messages.subject_clean: Simmer and hospital beds in two different wards
messages.body_plain:
Problem:
I have several questions relating to planning the capacity of a new postop ward A that is a supplement to an ICU ward B (6 beds). When the capacity of ward B is exhausted, ICU patients will be transferred to ward A and vice versa - but preferentially postop patients should be in A and ICU patients in A. However, the capacity of ward A depends on the day of week (mond-fri 10 beds, sat-sun 4 beds).

Question:
1-How can I model the spillover between the two wards?
2-How can i model the capacity difference in ward A during the week & weekend?

if the unit of time is days over a year - can I somehow calculate the number of days in a year where capacity is exceeded - i.e. queue >0- without creating a 1:365 vector and joining into it?

messages.body_plain:
On Wed, 28 Apr 2021 at 19:08, moleps islon <mol...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Problem:
> I have several questions relating to planning the capacity of a new postop ward A that is a supplement to an ICU ward B (6 beds). When the capacity of ward B is exhausted, ICU patients will be transferred to ward A and vice versa - but preferentially postop patients should be in A and ICU patients in A. However, the capacity of ward A depends on the day of week (mond-fri 10 beds, sat-sun 4 beds).
>
> Question:
> 1-How can I model the spillover between the two wards?

The seize() activity has a "reject" argument, which enables you to set
a trajectory to be followed when an arrival fails to seize the
resource. You can use this to transfer arrivals to the other ward.

> 2-How can i model the capacity difference in ward A during the week & weekend?

See the schedule() function. If the simulated time unit is the day,
your schedule would be:

> schedule(0:6, c(rep(10, 5), rep(4, 2)), period=7)
schedule: period: 7
{ timetable:  0  1  2  3  4  5  6 }
{ values:    10 10 10 10 10  4  4 }

> if the unit of time is days over a year - can I somehow calculate the number of days in a year where capacity is exceeded - i.e. queue >0- without creating a 1:365 vector and joining into it?

I would truncate the time column from get_mon_resources(), summarise
by day and count.

--
Iñaki Úcar

> See the schedule() function. If the simulated time unit is the day,

>

> schedule: period: 7
> { timetable:  0  1  2  3  4  5  6 }

Or even simpler than that:

> schedule(c(0, 5), c(10, 4), period=7)
schedule: period: 7
{ timetable:  0  5 }
{ values:    10  4 }

--
Iñaki Úcar
